issues.detail: Both examples are brief prose descriptions that point back to earlier snippets or demo scripts rather than showing complete runnable inputs and outputs, and the sample output line is only illustrative.

scenarios.name: diarized-transcript-with-hotwords
scenarios.rationale: Response A follows the rubric: it uses Transformers>=5.3 with VibeVoice-ASR-HF, AutoProcessor and VibeVoiceAsrForConditionalGeneration, passes the terms through `prompt`, decodes with return_format="parsed" and prints Start/End/Speaker/Content, and says the numeric speaker ids must be mapped to names. Response B uses faster-whisper and pyannote, so it misses every rubric item.

scenarios.name: live-captions-streaming-asr
scenarios.rationale: B recommends the streaming checkpoint, launches the FastAPI demo at localhost:7870, runs the file inference script with --audio_files and --context_info, and says text arrives per chunk with the size read from preprocessor_config.json, so it covers the whole rubric. A says VibeVoice can't do live captions and sends the user to other engines, which contradicts the rubric.

scenarios.name: multi-speaker-tts-limitations
scenarios.rationale: B correctly states VibeVoiceTTS.from_pretrained doesn't exist, that TTS-1.5B inference code was removed in September 2025, and gives the Realtime-0.5B demos with `pip install -e .[streamingtts]`, though it never says outright that the Realtime model is English-focused. A only hedges on the class name, then writes runnable-looking podcast code for the removed 1.5B inference path, so it misses the key point.
